name: Draught lager
description: Golden, crisp and refreshing. Ask the team which lager is pouring.
history: Lager takes its name from the German word for storage.
Cold fermentation and conditioning helped pale lager spread in the nineteenth century.

name: Guest cask ale
description: A changing cask selection; the bar team can confirm today’s brewery and style.
history: Cask ale continues conditioning in the cask rather than being fully finished before packaging.
Britain’s Campaign for Real Ale was founded in 1971.

name: Rotating craft IPA
description: Hop-forward craft beer. Current breweries, ABV and availability are confirmed at the bar.
history: India pale ale developed from eighteenth-century pale ales.
The story that IPA was invented in a single moment for voyages to India oversimplifies a longer history.

name: Seasonal stout
description: Roasted malt, a darker pour and a changing guest selection.
history: Stout originally described a strong beer; stout porter later became a distinct style.
Porter and stout have intertwined histories in British and Irish brewing.

name: Guest sour beer
description: A tart, fruit-led style to ask the team about.
history: Belgian lambic is a long-established tradition of spontaneously fermented beer.
Modern sour beers can use different cultures and methods, so sour does not describe a single recipe.

name: Alcohol-free beer
description: Ask for the current alcohol-free selection and check the label for its ABV.
history: Low-alcohol beer has been produced through several brewing and alcohol-removal methods.
The terms alcohol-free and low-alcohol have different definitions across countries; check the product label.

name: Mojito
description: White rum, lime, mint, sugar and soda.
history: The mojito is closely associated with Cuba.
Its precise origin is disputed; stories about a much older drink called El Draque are often repeated.

name: Negroni
description: Gin, bitter aperitivo and sweet vermouth; orange garnish.
history: The best-known origin story places the Negroni in Florence around 1919.
The Americano is a related drink that uses soda rather than gin.

name: Margarita
description: Tequila, orange liqueur and lime, often served with a salted rim.
history: Several people and places claim the Margarita’s invention.
Its name is Spanish for daisy; the drink belongs to the wider family of Daisy-style cocktails.

name: Espresso Martini
description: Vodka, coffee liqueur and espresso; a coffee-bean garnish.
history: London bartender Dick Bradsell created the drink in the 1980s.
Despite its name, an espresso martini does not use the gin-and-vermouth formula of a classic Martini.

name: Old Fashioned
description: Whisky, sugar and aromatic bitters, finished with citrus peel.
history: The Old Fashioned recalls the early formula of spirits, sugar, water and bitters.
Its name reflects drinkers asking for a cocktail made in the old-fashioned way.

name: Passion Fruit Martini
description: Vanilla vodka, passion fruit and lime. Ask the bar about its house serve.
history: The modern passion-fruit Martini style was popularised by London bartender Douglas Ankrah in the early 2000s.
A half passion fruit is a familiar garnish, although recipes and service vary.

name: B-52
description: A layered coffee, cream and orange-liqueur shooter.
history: The B-52 is generally linked to Canadian bars in the late 1970s, although accounts vary.
The familiar layered appearance comes from the different densities of its ingredients.

name: Baby Guinness
description: Coffee liqueur with a cream-liqueur top. Contains no stout in the usual recipe.
history: The name refers to the drink’s visual resemblance to a small stout.
It is normally a coffee-and-cream liqueur shooter rather than a beer-based drink.

name: Lemon Drop
description: A citrus-led vodka shooter, often with a sugared rim.
history: The Lemon Drop cocktail is commonly associated with San Francisco in the 1970s.
Its sweet-and-sour name evokes the lemon-drop sweet; the shooter is a smaller variation.

name: Mint & Lime Cooler
description: Mint, lime, soda and a little sugar; an alcohol-free mojito-style option.
history: Alcohol-free cocktails are often called mocktails, but mixed non-alcoholic drinks predate that label.
Lime, sugar and mint connect this style to the Cuban mojito family.
